'''Liette Vasseur''' (born 29 April 1963, in [[Laval, Quebec|Laval]], Quebec) is a [[Canadian]] [[biologist]] who has held the [[UNESCO]] Chair in ''Community Sustainability: From Local to Global'' in the Department of Biological Sciences since 2014 (renewed in 2018) at [[Brock University]] in [[St. Catharines|St. Catharines, Ontario]], [[Canada]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://scienceetbiencommun.pressbooks.pub/citoyennesdelaterre/chapter/liette-vasseur/|title=Liette Vasseur (1963), Québec – Citoyennes de la Terre|website=scienceetbiencommun.pressbooks.pub|access-date=2019-03-07}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://scienceetbiencommun.pressbooks.pub/citoyennesdelaterre/chapter/liette-vasseur/|title=Liette Vasseur (1963), Québec – Citoyennes de la Terre|website=scienceetbiencommun.pressbooks.pub|access-date=2019-03-07}}</ref> She is also a member of the Women and Gender Studies program and the Environmental Sustainability Research Centre.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://brocku.ca/brock-news/2019/02/international-research-shows-wasps-can-be-used-to-combat-agricultural-pests/|title=International research shows wasps can be used to combat agricultural pests|website=The Brock News, a news source for Brock University|language=en-CA|access-date=2019-03-07}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://brocku.ca/brock-news/2018/06/brock-biologist-named-president-of-canadian-commission-for-unesco/|title=Brock biologist named President of Canadian Commission for UNESCO|website=The Brock News, a news source for Brock University|language=en-CA|access-date=2019-03-07}}</ref>

== Childhood and education ==
Vasseur was born on April 29, 1963, on a farm in [[Laval, Quebec|Laval]], north of [[Montreal]].<ref name=":0" /> Her father and paternal grandfather were florists.<ref name=":3" />

Liette's primary studies began in 1969 at John XXIII School and Simon Vanier School. She did her first two years of secondary school at St-Martin and finally completed her third, fourth and fifth year at St-Maxime.<ref name=":1" /> She did her CEGEP at Ahuntsic College.

She graduated from [[Université de Sherbrooke|Sherbrooke University]] with a degree in biology and ecology. She graduated in 1985.<ref name=":1" />

Liette then studied biology at the [[Université du Québec à Montréal|University of Quebec in Montreal]] (UQAM) where she graduated in 1987. She then worked on the conservation of wild garlic. She was able to do part of a research team at the [[Université de Montréal]] in population genetics with Jean-Pierre Simon.<ref name=":1" />

She then completed her Ph.D. in biology at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] (Kingston, Ontario) and graduated in 1991. She eventually began a postdoctoral fellowship with Catherine Potvin at [[McGill University]].<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
Vasseur, who trained in Ecology has developed an interdisciplinary research programme with links to issues such as community-based ecosystem management, [[climate change adaptation]] and resilience and sustainable agriculture both nationally and internationally.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}}

In Canada, her research areas include impacts of climate change including extreme events on natural and managed ecosystems as well as rural communities, use of new alternatives in sustainable agriculture, and ecosystem/landscape sustainable development, conservation, and resilience in rural communities in Canada and abroad.<ref name=":2" />

She was part of the co-direction committee of a large project on Coastal Communities Challenges in the face of Climate Change, funded by the Social and Humanities Research Council of Canada, which looked at resilience and ecosystem-based adaptations in ten coastal communities of Atlantic Canada. &nbsp;

She also works in China, where she is a Minjiang Scholar at [[Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University]], and in [[Ecuador]], where she focuses on the community sustainability and ecosystem-based adaptation to climate change of rural native communities in the Andean region of the [[Chimborazo]]. &nbsp;

Vasseur has also been involved in projects in other countries such as Vietnam, Cambodia, Panama, Brazil, Burkina Faso, in Africa.

From 2018 to 2022 she was the President of the [[Canadian Commission for UNESCO]], where she was previously Chair of the Sectoral Commission on Social, Human and Natural Sciences.<ref name=":3" /> She is the vice-chair for North America on the steering committee of the Commission for Ecosystem Management at the International Union for Conservation of Nature and leads the thematic group on Ecosystem Governance.<ref name=":2" />

== Special interests ==
Vasseur is also very involved in issues related to women in science, engineering, trades and technology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.universityaffairs.ca/opinion/in-my-opinion/universities-should-embrace-womens-non-linear-career-paths/|title=Universities should embrace women's non-linear career paths|website=University Affairs|language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elliotlaketoday.com/local-news/beyond-local-are-universities-catering-only-to-young-students-1265537|title=BEYOND LOCAL: Are universities catering only to young students?|website=ElliotLakeToday.com|language=en|access-date=2019-03-07}}</ref> On this topic, she has produced several publications on this topic as well as organized some events and projects to promote gender equality.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://theconversation.com/supporting-mature-female-students-enrolling-in-university-stem-programs-111217|title=Supporting mature female students enrolling in university STEM programs|last=Vasseur|first=Liette|website=The Conversation|language=en|access-date=2019-03-07}}</ref> She is the Past-President (President from 2014 to 2018) of the Canadian Coalition of Women in Engineering, Science, Trades and Technology.
